title: refresh-report.json
description: The summary `python -m pipeline.refresh --report FILE` writes. The weekly workflow reads `status`, `reason` and `stale[]`; every other key is informational. Keys are only ever added, never renamed (tests/test_refresh.py pins this file).

status.description: failed means nothing was written; `reason` says why

reason.description: only when status is failed: the error, with the traceback tail for an unexpected one

changed.description: true when at least one file was written

lists.description: per list CSV: rows_before, rows_after, added, removed, status_changed, date_changed, other_changed, samples, page_date, source_rows, unchanged, stale

explained.description: file -> notes explaining a removal or other surprising change

fallback.description: paid fallback use: count, cost_usd, errors

stale.description: sources that could not be fetched this run and kept their last good data

since.description: ISO date of the newest retrieval the kept data carries; may be empty

age_days.description: run date minus since; null when since is unknown

escalate.description: true when age_days is null or more than 30: the workflow should raise the escalation label instead of only commenting
